tasks.title: Reconstruct a tabletop scene
tasks.sum: Recover a single 3D scene that explains photographs of objects arranged on a table.
tasks.in: RGB photographs without camera calibration, depth, or scene measurements. Blender, scene-building tools, and a package example are supplied.
tasks.out: One fixed Blender scene with geometry and materials, plus a camera estimate for every input image. All views must share the same scene and camera intrinsics.
tasks.ok: The evaluator compares object surfaces, rendered depth and appearance, and estimated cameras with fixed reference measurements after one shared scene registration.
tasks.score: Object surfaces contribute 35 points, depth 15, appearance 30, and camera recovery 20. Appearance includes the objects and visible table; missing surfaces remain errors.

inp.cap: All 6 input photos

tasks.title: Reconstruct a complex object
tasks.sum: Recover the shape and materials of a detailed object so it can be viewed from new directions.
tasks.in: Uncalibrated photographs of one complex object, with no depth or camera poses. Scene-building and preview tools are provided.
tasks.out: A fixed Blender scene and one estimated camera per image, with shared camera intrinsics.
tasks.ok: Reference surfaces and depth are used where the observations provide reliable support. Unseen rear surfaces are not treated as fully observed ground truth.
tasks.score: Surface agreement contributes 35 points, depth consistency 15, foreground appearance 30, and cameras 20. Missing predicted object regions lose credit.

inp.cap: All 6 input photos

tasks.title: Reconstruct a furnished room
tasks.sum: Build the room structure, furniture, and smaller objects visible in a set of photographs.
tasks.in: Room photographs without camera calibration or depth. Different photographs may have different camera intrinsics.
tasks.out: One Blender scene containing the observable room and its contents, plus a camera estimate for each photograph.
tasks.ok: Reference scan geometry and supported image regions define the comparison. The scene and all cameras use one shared registration.
tasks.score: Surface agreement contributes 35 points, depth 15, appearance 30, and cameras 20. Geometry balances structure, furniture, and small objects so large walls do not dominate.

inp.cap: 6 of the 16 input photos

brief.p: Reconstruct the {whole observable room}, including architecture, furniture, fixtures and small objects. Use the supplied multiview RGB images to reconstruct geometry, materials and lighting. … {No camera calibration, poses, depth or scene measurements are supplied.}
brief.sc: Surface geometry, appearance in held-out photo views, and the estimated cameras
brief.cap: Sixteen uncalibrated wide-angle photos of one furnished room

tasks.title: Reconstruct two people in a fixed pose
tasks.sum: Recover two people's clothed surfaces, body fits, and relative positions from photographs.
tasks.in: Uncalibrated photographs, generic SMPL-X body models, and tools for binding body fits to scene meshes. Target body parameters are not supplied.
tasks.out: A Blender scene, a fitted SMPL-X body and mesh binding for each person, and independent camera intrinsics and poses for each image.
tasks.ok: Clothed surfaces, silhouettes, appearance, and fitted reference bodies are compared after one scene registration. The body reference is a fit, not direct physical joint ground truth.
tasks.score: Clothed surfaces contribute 25 points, anatomical body fit 15, silhouettes 10, appearance 30, and cameras 20. Missing or extra people reduce credit.

inp.cap: All 6 input photos

tasks.title: Reconstruct an outdoor scene
tasks.sum: Rebuild visible terrain, vegetation, rocks, water appearance, and atmosphere from photographs.
tasks.in: Uncalibrated RGB images of a static outdoor scene, without depth or camera poses.
tasks.out: One fixed Blender scene with geometry, materials, and atmospheric appearance, plus cameras with shared intrinsics.
tasks.ok: Reliable surface and depth regions support geometry checks. Sky, water, reflections, and fog remain part of the image comparison even where depth is ambiguous.
tasks.score: Surfaces contribute 35 points, depth 15, appearance 30, and camera recovery 20. Geometry balances terrain, trees and wood, and rocks and understory.

inp.cap: 6 of the 16 input photos

tasks.title: Reconstruct objects and continuous motion
tasks.sum: Recover the geometry, appearance, and motion of objects from sparse timed views.
tasks.in: Calibrated RGB images and timestamps, with one or two views at each acquisition time. Generic assets and motion constraints are supplied.
tasks.out: A numeric scene containing edited geometry, materials, and continuous animation using the specified motion knots and interpolation rules.
tasks.ok: Geometry and motion are checked in the supplied metric world frame. Evaluation includes new views and times where reference support is available; supplied fixed surroundings earn no credit.
tasks.score: Surfaces contribute 35 points, RGB appearance 22.5, silhouettes 7.5, world-space state 20, and temporal consistency 15. No fitted global alignment is applied.

inp.cap: 6 of the 19 input images

tasks.title: Reconstruct a ball, block, and domino sequence
tasks.sum: Recover the shapes and continuous motion of objects that collide and move together.
tasks.in: Calibrated, timestamped views of a ball, impact block, and dominoes, plus fixed surroundings and public contact and gravity priors.
tasks.out: A numeric scene with object geometry, materials, and continuous animation. Authored animation is allowed; a physics solver is not required.
tasks.ok: The evaluator checks the observed motion and supported contact relationships, including contact timing, separation, penetration, and support. The supplied table and track are not reconstruction targets.
tasks.score: Surfaces contribute 35 points, RGB 22.5, silhouettes 7.5, state 20, temporal consistency 10, and interaction agreement 5.

inp.cap: 6 of the 144 input images

tasks.title: Reconstruct hands manipulating a hinged object
tasks.sum: Recover two hands and an articulated object throughout a manipulation sequence.
tasks.in: Calibrated photographs with timestamps, generic hand templates and rigs, shape bases, and an editable object mesh.
tasks.out: A numeric scene with animated hands and object, supported materials, and the required hand topology and articulation.
tasks.ok: Reviewed image measurements define silhouettes, hand landmarks, object fiducials, and which surface appears in front. They do not establish complete 3D hand geometry or contact forces.
tasks.score: Silhouettes contribute 35 points, appearance 30, state 20, temporal consistency 10, and front–back ordering 5. Incorrect ownership of foreground pixels is penalized.

inp.cap: 6 of the 64 input images

tasks.title: Reconstruct two people in motion
tasks.sum: Rebuild two people's changing shape, clothing appearance, and motion across time.
tasks.in: Calibrated, timestamped photographs and optional generic body models. Agents may use their own meshes and rigs.
tasks.out: An animated numeric scene with both people and wrist landmarks bound to rendered surface patches. Background reconstruction is outside the task.
tasks.ok: Reviewed image evidence supports silhouettes, foreground appearance, wrist positions, and occlusion order. It is not an exact 3D surface or contact-force reference.
tasks.score: Silhouettes contribute 35 points, appearance 30, wrist reprojection 20, wrist temporal consistency 10, and front–back ordering 5. Landmark measurements include their declared uncertainty allowance.

inp.cap: 6 of the 96 input images

tasks.title: Reconstruct a moving traffic scene
tasks.sum: Recover moving traffic participants and the surrounding observable scene.
tasks.in: Calibrated image streams from five cameras, exposure timestamps, generic target assets, and the scene contract.
tasks.out: A numeric scene with traffic-participant geometry, appearance, continuous trajectories, and required static context.
tasks.ok: Associated LiDAR points, annotated object states, images, and occlusion measurements provide the reference. LiDAR support does not fully specify empty space or every hidden surface.
tasks.score: Moving-target and context geometry contribute 25 and 10 points; their appearance terms contribute 15 each. State, temporal consistency, and occlusion ordering contribute 20, 10, and 5.

inp.cap: 6 of the 160 input images

brief.p: Reconstruct the target objects' {geometry, appearance and continuous motion} from the calibrated images in observations.json. … assets.json contains {generic starting templates, not the exact target shapes}. … Reconstruct the surrounding static scene inside the declared context bounds.
brief.sc: Shape, look and motion against held-out LiDAR, photos and vehicle boxes
brief.cap: Five calibrated on-vehicle camera streams (160 photos, 6 s), generic car boxes

tasks.title: Build a rocky trail landscape
tasks.sum: Turn dimensions, planting requirements, and reference images into a complete landscape scene.
tasks.in: Terrain and trail requirements, dimensions, planting specifications, and images of selected rocks, deadwood, and shrubs.
tasks.out: A Blender scene with terrain, soil base and skirt, rocks, deadwood, shrubs, and groundcover, with every required component identified.
tasks.ok: Public construction requirements define layout and clearances. Supplied component images define appearance; support, embedment, and skirt continuity are checked geometrically.
tasks.score: Layout and required content contribute 40 points, selected-component appearance 30, and construction constraints 30. Appearance is scored on ten specified components, not on every surface.

inp.cap: 6 of the 13 reference images

tasks.title: Build a furnished workshop
tasks.sum: Construct a complete workshop from architectural drawings and furnishing schedules.
tasks.in: Dimensioned plans, elevations, sections, furnishing and finish schedules, and component appearance images.
tasks.out: A Blender scene containing the room shell, openings, furniture, tools, and lighting, with required assemblies mapped by name.
tasks.ok: Plans define layout and completeness. Images define the appearance of the bookshelf, workbench, stool, and tool chest; geometric checks test support, penetration, and clearance.
tasks.score: Layout and completeness contribute 40 points, selected-furniture appearance 30, and construction checks 30. Support checks are geometric screens, not proofs of mechanical stability.

inp.cap: All 4 reference images

tasks.title: Build a pose-configurable humanoid
tasks.sum: Reconstruct a humanoid robot whose exterior responds correctly to pose controls.
tasks.in: Drawings, construction details, and calibrated neutral and posed images, with specifications for 29 body controls and six root controls.
tasks.out: A native Blender scene with exterior geometry, materials, and mapped controls that the evaluator can set.
tasks.ok: The exterior and its response across prescribed configurations are compared with reference measurements. Locomotion, balance, hidden interior parts, and exact rig topology are outside scope.
tasks.score: Exterior surfaces contribute 30 points, structural profiles 10, appearance 30, and control response 30. Control response measures how component surface positions and shapes change.

inp.cap: All 5 reference images

tasks.title: Animate a twirling dress from sketches
tasks.sum: Create a connected dress surface that turns, deforms, and settles across three motion scenarios.
tasks.in: Neutral drawings, timestamped turning and stopping panels, dimensions, support motion, texture, and camera calibration.
tasks.out: A Blender scene with one fixed-topology dress mesh and animated deformation. Baked animation is allowed; a live cloth solver is optional.
tasks.ok: The result is compared with reference shape and appearance, including times between panels. Sparse sketches allow multiple plausible completions, so the reference is not a uniquely determined solution.
tasks.score: Surface agreement contributes 40 points, appearance 30, and behavior 30. Behavior covers deformation, attachment, continuity, settling, and differences between scenarios.

inp.cap: All 6 reference images

brief.p: Build and animate the printed open-surface dress in Blender 4.5.3 LTS. … {No garment mesh, dense posed 3D surfaces, cloth settings or deformation recipe is supplied.} … {Hidden folds/intermediate motion are not uniquely determined by the sketches}; reference agreement is a stronger objective than plausibility.
brief.sc: Surface (40) and appearance (30) vs a hidden reference; motion behaviour (30)
brief.cap: Three shape drawings, fifteen motion sketches, dimensions and the print design

tasks.title: Reconstruct and rig a galloping horse
tasks.sum: Build the pictured horse and animate its gallop through a working armature.
tasks.in: Calibrated neutral images, body-part masks, surface anchors, posed motion targets, and hoof-contact annotations.
tasks.out: Body, hair, and eye meshes driven by one shared armature in Blender. Shape keys and mesh-cache animation cannot replace the rig.
tasks.ok: Images, semantic parts, landmarks, and contact annotations define the target. Exact hidden 3D geometry or an identical rig is not required.
tasks.score: Semantic masks contribute 40 points, appearance 30, and behavior 30. Behavior tests keypoints, deformation, temporal continuity, hoof contact, and whether the armature actually drives the motion.

inp.cap: 6 of the 8 reference images

tasks.title: Model a plant bending under force
tasks.sum: Infer a plant's deformable response and predict its motion under new force programs.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstration videos with force histories, plant geometry, fixed support, rest shape, and force-application patches.
tasks.out: A reusable simulator that returns displacements and velocities at requested material sites. The agent chooses its material model and discretization.
tasks.ok: Withheld response trajectories test bending and motion under other forces. Collision and self-contact are excluded; matching the response does not require recovering the reference implementation.
tasks.score: Position errors at 1,024 material points are averaged across six time phases. Each case scores the lowest-quality quarter of points; the final score averages 12 cases.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

brief.p: Build one reusable simulator for the supplied system and new prescribed controls. … {Internal discretization, material/mass law and response model}; {no hidden coefficients or numeric demo trajectories}. … All prescribed controls may be supplied; reference response trajectories remain private.
brief.sc: 3D position error of 1,024 surface points on 12 unseen force programs
brief.cap: Plant surface, supports and force programs; six demonstrations as video only

tasks.title: Model a pneumatic motion platform
tasks.sum: Predict platform motion and gas pressures when six pneumatic cylinders are driven by valve commands.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstrations, valve commands, geometry, masses, inertias, gas-network connections, gas constants, and reset conditions.
tasks.out: A simulator returning platform position and orientation and three reservoir pressures at requested times.
tasks.ok: Withheld trajectories test the inferred flow restrictions, heat exchange, and dissipative response under other valve programs.
tasks.score: Six platform-mount positions share half the observation weight and three pressures share half. Errors balance active and sealed phases; the lowest-quality quarter of observation weight is averaged over 12 cases.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

tasks.title: Model cloth pulled at two points
tasks.sum: Infer a hanging cloth's properties and predict its response to moving attachment targets.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstration videos, target trajectories, spring-attachment constants, contact configuration, and numerical support.
tasks.out: A simulator returning the positions of 289 fixed material sites. The agent infers rest shape, initial sag, density, elasticity, and damping.
tasks.ok: Withheld cloth trajectories test the response to other target motions. The output sites preserve material correspondence even while the cloth deforms.
tasks.score: Position errors give equal weight to the initial, manipulation, and subsequent-response phases. Each case scores the lowest-quality quarter of sites; scores are averaged across 12 cases.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

tasks.title: Model water driven by two pistons
tasks.sum: Predict how water moves in a tank under prescribed piston motions.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstrations, tank geometry, two piston-motion programs, and an exact sample representation of the initial water volume.
tasks.out: A simulator returning water-sample positions and nonnegative volume weights at requested times. Particle identities and sampling density may change.
tasks.ok: Predicted and reference water volumes are compared spatially on the same grid. The evaluator measures occupied volume rather than matching particle identities.
tasks.score: Volume discrepancies are averaged over time in 20 longitudinal bands. The worst-quality quarter of bands determines each case score, averaged over 12 cases; incorrect total volume is not normalized away.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

tasks.title: Model a multi-gyroscope assembly
tasks.sum: Recover the dynamics of a carrier, three gimbals, and three rotors from their visible response.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstrations, assembly geometry, joints, gravity, initial conditions, and four torque-input programs.
tasks.out: A reusable multibody simulator predicting the poses of all seven bodies. Masses, centers of mass, inertias, and dissipation must be inferred.
tasks.ok: Withheld pose trajectories test how the whole assembly responds to other torque programs.
tasks.score: Position and rotation errors are combined per body and balanced across six control phases. The two lowest-quality bodies determine each case score; 12 cases are averaged.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

tasks.title: Model rigid-body contact and friction
tasks.sum: Make supplied rigid bodies interact correctly with a table, fences, and a moving pusher.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstrations, exact geometry and mass properties, free-body dynamics, initial states, and pusher trajectories.
tasks.out: A simulator implementing contact, friction, and numerical updates, and returning body poses plus linear and angular velocities.
tasks.ok: Withheld trajectories measure the motion produced by the missing interactions. The known individual-body mechanics are supplied.
tasks.score: Each responsive body contributes 256 surface sites. Position errors are averaged over the control sequence with the specified symmetry handling; the lowest-quality quarter of sites is averaged across 12 cases.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

brief.p: Predict the coupled response under supplied controls. … {Contact construction and release, modes/history, reciprocal forces/moments and joint response}; equivalent complete simulators are allowed. … Use only the supplied public observations, controls, geometry and reset; {no private reference trajectories or parameters}.
brief.sc: 3D position error of 256 surface points per body on 12 unseen pusher programs
brief.cap: Body shapes, masses and pusher controls; six demonstrations as video only

tasks.title: Model cloth carrying an object
tasks.sum: Implement the contacts that let a moving cloth carry a box, cylinder, or ellipsoid above a table.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstrations, cloth and rigid-body mechanics, geometry queries, and a fixed joint implicit solver.
tasks.out: A contact plugin providing normal and friction forces and the required derivatives for cloth, object, table, and self-contact. The supplied mechanics and solver must be preserved.
tasks.ok: Withheld motion checks whether reciprocal contact forces produce the correct cloth shape and object transport.
tasks.score: Cloth sites and object surface vertices each receive half the observation weight. Future-time position errors feed one lowest-quarter weighted score per case, averaged over 12 cases.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

tasks.title: Model chain engagement and tensioning
tasks.sum: Make a compliant chain transfer motion between driven and passive wheels.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstrations, geometry, component mechanics, initial conditions, torque and brake programs, and optional integration support.
tasks.out: A simulator implementing chain–wheel engagement and reciprocal forces, returning chain-node positions, shaft angles, and passive-idler position.
tasks.ok: Withheld trajectories test engagement, motion transfer, and passive tensioning under other drive and brake commands.
tasks.score: Chain nodes, input shaft, output shaft, and idler receive equal group weight. Errors include event-centered and rolling windows; the lowest-quality quarter of weight is averaged over 12 cases.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

tasks.title: Model a quadruped towing a cart
tasks.sum: Reproduce robot and cart motion by supplying their missing ground and hitch interactions.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstrations, motor commands, and a contact-disabled library providing articulated dynamics, geometry, actuators, and passive joints.
tasks.out: A simulator applying foot, wheel, body, and tow-hitch forces through the supplied component dynamics, returning generalized positions and velocities.
tasks.ok: Withheld response trajectories test how contact and towing forces couple the robot to the passive cart.
tasks.score: Surface-position errors cover robot body, feet, cart chassis, and wheels with equal group weight. The lowest-quality quarter of weight is averaged over 12 cases; irrelevant axial wheel spin is ignored.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

tasks.title: Model fluid and floating bodies together
tasks.sum: Couple piston-driven water with three floating rigid bodies so both affect each other.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstrations, geometry, masses, gravity, reset conditions, and supplied fluid and free-body dynamics.
tasks.out: Plugins for moving fluid boundaries, reciprocal forces and torques, and rigid contact, producing body states and water samples with volume and velocity.
tasks.ok: Withheld trajectories compare body motion and the water's spatial volume and velocity distributions. Walls and prescribed pistons are not scored objects.
tasks.score: Body-surface positions receive half the weight, fluid volume one quarter, and fluid velocity one quarter. Time-averaged errors feed a lowest-quarter weighted score across 12 cases.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

tasks.title: Model compaction after repeated impacts
tasks.sum: Predict how a material block's loading history changes its later response.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstrations, impactor controls, initial material geometry and preparation, reversible response, rigid dynamics, and contact coupling.
tasks.out: A simulator with persistent material state, returning material-site positions and impactor states throughout the complete loading history.
tasks.ok: Withheld histories test both accumulated deformation and the response to a final probe. Resetting the material between impacts would lose the required memory.
tasks.score: Material and impactor surface points are pooled. Errors balance history and probe phases where applicable; the lowest-quality quarter of points is averaged over 12 cases.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

tasks.title: Model a sheet's bending and twisting history
tasks.sum: Predict deformation and residual shape after a sheet undergoes a sequence of loads.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstrations, clamped-sheet geometry, elastic constants, force mapping, initial conditions, and a fixed structural solver.
tasks.out: A material module mapping strain and previous state to stress, tangent, and candidate state. History is committed only after a solver step converges.
tasks.ok: Withheld trajectories test loading history, later probe response, and residual deformation while using the same structural solver.
tasks.score: Position errors at 2,673 sites balance six spatial regions. History, probe phases, and the final residual shape each receive one third of temporal weight; lowest-quarter scores are averaged over 12 cases.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

brief.p: Infer a reusable material response with {persistent internal state} from clean, calibrated RGB demonstrations and complete known force histories. Predict the sheet's full response under new loading histories, including reversals, local probe response and {permanent shape after unloading}.
brief.sc: Surface positions over a new force history; the unloaded shape weighs most
brief.cap: Six demo histories as 3-view videos with full force records, plus the solver

tasks.title: Model tires with evolving pressure and heat
tasks.sum: Predict how driving and air leaks change tire response and subsequent vehicle motion.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstrations, driving and leak-opening commands, and a nominal vehicle model handling steering, drive, braking, and integration.
tasks.out: A persistent response module coupling gas mass, temperature, tire compression, stiffness, and rolling resistance within the supplied vehicle model.
tasks.ok: Withheld driving histories test effects that continue after a leak closes. Physical loading time follows the declared simulation clock, not video playback speed.
tasks.score: Planar chassis-position and heading errors each balance history and probe phases. The worse normalized channel determines each lowest-quarter score, averaged over 12 cases.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

tasks.title: Model structural deterioration across earthquakes
tasks.sum: Predict a three-story frame's response to a mainshock and later shaking without resetting its damage history.
tasks.in: Six calibrated demonstrations, ground-motion inputs, frame geometry, masses, elastic members, constraints, gravity, damping, and integration support.
tasks.out: A stateful rotational-joint model or compatible simulator returning nodal translations and rotations across the complete sequence.
tasks.ok: Withheld motion trajectories test how earlier loading changes later response. Damage labels themselves are not scored.
tasks.score: Columns, beams, and floors receive equal observation weight. Ground-relative position errors balance earlier and later phases; the lowest-quality quarter of weight is averaged over 12 cases.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

tasks.title: Model permanent stretching of a thin sheet
tasks.sum: Predict irreversible in-plane deformation as a sheet is loaded, unloaded, and loaded again.
tasks.in: Six complete demonstrations from two calibrated views, a fixed equilibrium solver, and a mesh. During development, the agent also sees the full loading program and preparation videos for each of the twelve evaluation cases.
tasks.out: A stateful material module initialized from the flat sheet, preserving history through the solver's trial and commit interface.
tasks.ok: After the preparation phase, the sheet’s deformation during loading and unloading and its residual shape are withheld for scoring. The task excludes fracture, contact, gravity, inertia, rate dependence, and permanent bending.
tasks.score: Position errors at 289 nodes use rest-area weights and balance loaded, unloading, and fully unloaded phases. Lowest-quarter scores are averaged over 12 cases; incomplete equilibrium trajectories score zero.

inp.cap: One of the six public demonstrations

tasks.title: Replace a mixer drivetrain
tasks.sum: Use two dexterous arms to open a mixer, exchange its drivetrain assembly, and close it safely.
tasks.in: A live simulator with RGB cameras, own-body instruments, finite-effort joint controls, and the public robot geometry and sensor calibration.
tasks.out: Actions in one continuous episode, chosen directly or by helper programs. The agent cannot reset or replay the world.
tasks.ok: Success requires the replacement installed, old assembly in its tray, lid closed, hands clear, and a quiet one-second hold. The assembly is exchanged as one rigid unit.
tasks.score: Four retained checkpoints award up to 60 points. Full success unlocks up to 40 additional points for action efficiency; the live episode is the evaluated execution.

inp.cap: The scene handed to the agent

tasks.title: Get a humanoid up from the floor
tasks.sum: Control a prone humanoid until it stands stably on its feet without external support.
tasks.in: Head-camera RGB, joint and inertial readings, sole and palm instruments, and control of all 43 actuated joints. Global pose and external views are unavailable.
tasks.out: Actions in one continuing live episode. Falls can be recovered from, but the world cannot be reset.
tasks.ok: Success requires two seconds of upright, feet-only support within the task's height, tilt, and velocity bounds.
tasks.score: Four retained posture milestones contribute up to 60 points. Full success unlocks up to 40 efficiency points, with recovery and holding actions included in the action count.

inp.cap: The scene handed to the agent

tasks.title: Reverse a two-trailer truck into a bay
tasks.sum: Dock a tractor and two trailers in the marked lane and bring the complete vehicle to rest.
tasks.in: Three vehicle-camera views and permitted instruments, without global pose or direct articulation-angle measurements.
tasks.out: Adaptive driving actions in one live episode without reset or rewind.
tasks.ok: Success requires the rear hitch correctly positioned and aligned, both trailers inside the lane, and all three bodies stationary for one second.
tasks.score: Five retained checkpoints contribute up to 60 points. Full success unlocks up to 40 action-efficiency points; contact does not erase previously earned checkpoints.

inp.cap: The scene handed to the agent

tasks.title: Recover equipment with two mobile robots
tasks.sum: Move three floor-standing devices into their matching marked docks.
tasks.in: Head and wrist RGB, encoders, local contact sensors, and controls for two mobile manipulators.
tasks.out: Coordinated actions in one live episode. Devices may be pushed, pulled, or grasped, in any order and with any division of labor.
tasks.ok: Each entire device base must lie inside its dock's inner boundary. Success additionally requires release from robot contact and two seconds of simultaneous stability.
tasks.score: Three current placement conditions contribute up to 60 points; credit is lost if a device leaves its dock. Full success unlocks up to 40 action-efficiency points.

inp.cap: The scene handed to the agent

brief.p: Recover T1, T2 and T3 into their matching visible docks. The entire base of each device must lie {inside the inner edge of the dock line without touching it}. … One agent controls both Fetch robots. … {No depth, map, external poses or external-object identity sensor is supplied.}
brief.sc: Each device fully inside its dock at the end, plus a bonus for few actions
brief.cap: Onboard RGB, encoders and contact readings of two robots; one live episode

tasks.title: Send a ball through three holes
tasks.sum: Use a fixed-leg humanoid's upper body and paddle to pass a ball through three wall holes in order.
tasks.in: Head and wrist RGB, joint and actuator readings, upper-body controls, and a ball-refresh command.
tasks.out: Actions in one continuing live episode. Refreshing the ball starts another attempt without resetting the robot or clock.
tasks.ok: The whole ball must pass from front to back through each hole's wall thickness in the prescribed order. The method of passage is unrestricted.
tasks.score: Three retained hole-passage checkpoints contribute up to 60 points. Completing all three unlocks up to 40 efficiency points; successful ball refreshes count as actions.

inp.cap: The scene handed to the agent

tasks.title: Route and lock a keyed cable
tasks.sum: Use two arms to route a cable through two slots, seat its plug, and lock the collar.
tasks.in: Table and wrist RGB, joint readings, wrist wrenches, local pad loads, and a deterministic scene that can be reset during development.
tasks.out: A fixed action sequence, replayed from the prescribed initial state without observation-dependent corrections.
tasks.ok: Both routing conditions, plug seating, and collar locking must hold at the end of replay. Releasing the cable or holding after release is not required.
tasks.score: Four current assembly checkpoints contribute up to 60 points. Full success unlocks up to 40 efficiency points based only on replay actions, not development attempts.

inp.cap: The scene handed to the agent

brief.p: Place cable inside A and B slots in either order, {seat the plug and mechanically lock the collar}. … Final evaluation replays only the frozen actions from a fresh initial state. … Aim to complete the entire task within the available time {using as few control actions as possible}.
brief.sc: End state of the replayed sequence: four checkpoints, plus efficiency on success
brief.cap: A fixed two-arm scene in a resettable simulator, with cameras and joint sensors

tasks.title: Lift a box onto a shelf
tasks.sum: Make a humanoid lift a four-kilogram box, place it on an upper shelf, and withdraw its hands.
tasks.in: Head and wrist RGB, joint and inertial readings, local contact instruments, and a resettable development scene.
tasks.out: A fixed action sequence that completes the task when independently replayed from the initial state.
tasks.ok: The shelf must carry at least 80% of the box's weight, both hands must clear, and the robot and box must satisfy the final stability checks.
tasks.score: Three historical stages contribute up to 60 points. Up to 40 action-efficiency points require full final success; a temporary shelf placement can earn progress without completing the task.

inp.cap: The scene handed to the agent

tasks.title: Land an unpowered aircraft
tasks.sum: Fly an unpowered approach in crosswind, land northbound in the marked zone, and stop legally.
tasks.in: Aircraft observations and flight instruments, six control channels, fixed terrain, constant crosswind, and resettable development trials.
tasks.out: A fixed control sequence covering approach, touchdown, and deceleration, evaluated by independent replay.
tasks.ok: The first-wheel touchdown location and touchdown quality must meet the landing conditions. The final ground state must also satisfy the stopping constraints.
tasks.score: Three checkpoints contribute up to 60 points, retaining touchdown events while checking the final stop. Full success unlocks up to 40 replay-action efficiency points.

inp.cap: The scene handed to the agent

tasks.title: Install a beam with a crane
tasks.sum: Place a beam on its matching supports, detach the crane hook, and move the hook clear.
tasks.in: Two RGB views, crane instruments and controls, and a resettable development scene. Direct beam and hook poses and contact identities are unavailable.
tasks.out: A fixed action sequence for replay from the prescribed initial state, including the final holding interval.
tasks.ok: The beam ends must rest on their color-matched supports without crane support. The detached hook must remain clear and the aligned configuration quiet for the final two seconds.
tasks.score: Four current support and release checkpoints contribute up to 60 points. Full success unlocks up to 40 replay-action efficiency points.

inp.cap: The scene handed to the agent

tasks.title: Pass through two interlocked doors
tasks.sum: Move a dual-arm mobile robot through two doors and leave the passage closed behind it.
tasks.in: RGB observations, proprioception, robot controls, and a resettable scene. The second door unlocks only after the first closes.
tasks.out: A fixed action sequence that independently replays both door operations and the final parking maneuver.
tasks.ok: The whole chassis must finish inside the goal, both doors closed and latched, arms in travel posture, and the robot stopped for one second.
tasks.score: Passage events and final-state conditions contribute up to 60 points. Full success unlocks up to 40 replay-action efficiency points; passing both doorways alone is insufficient.

inp.cap: The scene handed to the agent

tasks.title: Reorient a cuboid within a robot hand
tasks.sum: Write a policy that turns a marked cuboid to the required orientation and holds it steady.
tasks.in: Three RGB views, joint and actuator readings, local normal-force channels, and three development cases with different initial faces and yaw angles.
tasks.out: One frozen observation-dependent policy that runs autonomously on new cases, without resets or coding-agent intervention.
tasks.ok: The blue face must point upward and the white arrow north, with the object stable for the final two seconds. Palm contact is allowed.
tasks.score: Flip, turn, and stability conditions contribute up to 60 points per case; full success unlocks up to 40 action-efficiency points. The task score averages three hidden cases.

tasks.out: One autonomous policy that handles changes in doorway width, turn direction, distances, and corridor length.
tasks.ok: The whole robot and box must reach the goal while maintaining the grasp. Dropping the load, falling, or breaking passage rules ends the case.
tasks.score: Retained doorway and corner progress and final arrival contribute up to 60 points. Full success unlocks up to 40 efficiency points; scores are averaged over three hidden cases.

tasks.ok: Alignment, physical capture, and stable locking must hold at the end. The docked configuration must remain stable for the final two seconds.
tasks.score: Three final-state checkpoints contribute up to 60 points per case. Full success unlocks up to 40 action-efficiency points; scores are averaged over three hidden cases.

tasks.title: Deliver a suspended load through gates
